On Sun, 22 Mar 2026 at 09:12, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Thanks all — Alex finished onsite this morning. I captured a quick scorecard and attached it...

Short version: strong hire. My notes:
- Design (5/5): Clear tradeoff discussion on multi-region KV cache, proposed evacuation plan for a corrupted shard — concrete steps and rollback criteria.
- Execution (4/5): Implemented a prototype in the session, asked good clarifying Qs.
- On-call (3/5): Alex has runbooks and pager experience, but the examples were primarily SRE-style escalations rather than product-ownering incidents.
- Leadership (4/5): Communicates clearly, pushed for follow-up with product during the loop.

Evidence bullets: shipped a low-latency routing change for a regional cache in prior role (reduced tail latency; shared metrics), took ownership of a 2-day incident and coordinated two teams.

My recommendation: hire. If we proceed, prioritize a 2nd-round follow-up focused on ownership during high-severity incidents (15–20 min).

Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the write-up. I did a deeper dive on the on-call thread Alex shared during the interview (attached as oncall_log_excerpts.txt). Two concerns from my side:
1) The on-call examples were mostly firefighting tickets rather than ownership of service-level decisions (no evidence of retro/action items that changed practice).
2) When pushed on triage decisions under pressure, Alex defaulted to escalation rather than automation or permanent mitigation steps.

Given our upcoming push on reliability SLAs, I lean toward "needs-more-evidence" — specifically, a short (20 min) focused call asking for a concrete post-incident plan they owned and what they changed afterward. That would resolve my main signal.

Note: my overall technical evaluation is positive; this is narrowly about long-term ownership fit.

Aditya Rao
Staff Engineer, Infra
